Between the Sheets

cocktails.method:

cocktails.name: Bloody Mary

ingredients.ingredient: Tabasco, Celery Salt, Pepper (Up to taste)
ingredients.original: Tabasco, Celery Salt, Pepper (Up to taste)

cocktails.method:
Stir gently all the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice, pour into rocks glass.\nNOTE:
If requested served with ice, pour into highball glass.\nCelery, lemon wedge (Optional).

cocktails.name: Boulevardier
cocktails.method: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes.\nStir well. Strain into chilled cocktail glass.\nGarnish with a orange zest, optionally a lemon zest.
cocktails.garnish: Garnish with a orange zest, optionally a lemon zest.

cocktails.name: Bramble
cocktails.method: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker except the Crème de Mûre, shake well with ice, strain into chilled old fashioned glass filled with crushed ice, then pour the blackberry liqueur (Crème de Mûre) over the top of the drink, in a circular motion.\nGarnish optionally with a lemon slice and blackberries.
cocktails.garnish: Garnish optionally with a lemon slice and blackberries.

cocktails.name: Brandy Crusta
cocktails.method:
Mix together all ingredients with ice cubes in a mixing
glass and strain into a prepared slim cocktail glass.
Rub a slice of orange (or lemon) around the rim of the glass and dip it in
pulverized white sugar, so that the sugar will adhere to the edge of the glass.
Carefully curling place the orange/lemon peel around the inside of the glass.
cocktails.garnish: Rub a slice of orange (or lemon) around the rim of the glass and dip it in\npulverized white sugar, so that the sugar will adhere to the edge of the glass.\nCarefully curling place the orange/lemon peel around the inside of the glass.

cocktails.name: Caipirinha
cocktails.method:
Place lime and sugar into a double old fashioned glass and muddle gently.\nFill the glass with cracked ice and add Cachaça. Stir gently to involve ingredients.\nNote:
Caipiroska – Instead of Cachaça use Vodka;
Caipirissima – Instead of Cachaça use Rum.
Caipirão – Instead of Cachaça use Licor Beirão.\nN/A

cocktails.name: Canchanchara
cocktails.method:
Mix honey with water and lime juice and spread the mixture on the bottom and sides of the glass.
Add cracked ice, and then the rum.
End by energetically stirring from bottom to top.
Garnish with a lime wedge.

cocktails.name: Cardinale
cocktails.method: Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes. Stir well.\nStrain into chilled cocktail glass.\nGarnish with a lemon zest.

cocktails.garnish: Garnish with mint leaves and grated nutmeg.

cocktails.name: Clover Club

cocktails.name: Cuba Libre

cocktails.name: Irish Coffee
cocktails.method:
Warm black coffee is poured into a preheated Irish coffee glass.
Whiskey and at least one teaspoon of sugar is added and stirred until dissolved.
Fresh thick chilled cream is carefully poured over the back of a spoon held just above the surface of the coffee.
The layer of cream will float on the coffee without mixing.
Plain sugar can be replaced with sugar syrup

pour into a large glass and serve with straws.

cocktails.method: Pour all ingredients into cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, double strain into a large chilled cocktail glass.\nAccompany with a shot of champagne.\nGarnish with passion fruit cup and sugar.

cocktails.name: Ramos Fizz
cocktails.method:
Pour all ingredients except soda water in a cocktail shaker with ice.
Shake for two minutes, double strain in a glass, pour the drink back in the shaker and hard shake without ice for one minute.
Strain into a highball glass, top up with soda.
NOTE:
The drink was invented by Henry Ramos in 1888, at his bar Meyer’s Table d’Hôtel Internationale in New Orleans.
The Ramos Fizz was originally shaken for 12 minutes by a crew of 30 bartenders who passed the shaker from one to another.

Add the other ingredients to a mixing glass and fill it 3/4 full with ice. Stir until chilled, then strain into the glass rinsed with the absinthe.\nGarnish with lemon zest.

cocktails.name: Rusty Nail

cocktails.name: Sazerac
cocktails.method:
Rinse a chilled old-fashioned glass with the absinthe, add crushed ice and set it aside. Stir the remaining ingredients over ice in a mixing glass.
Discard the ice and any excess absinthe from the prepared glass, strain the mixed drink into the glass.
NOTE:
The original recipe changed after the American Civil War, Rye Whiskey substituted Cognac as it became hard to obtain.
Garnish with lemon zest.
